# Review: Bondarchuk, *Transfer of Training in Sports* Vol I, Chapters 1-2 (round 1, Opus)

Reviewer: independent round-1 reviewer (Opus), 2026-09-27. Scope: all 19 entries in
`staging/library/strength-and-conditioning/transfer-of-training-in-sports--bondarchuk/`.
Read-only on entries and source.

**Method.** Source: the Yessis text PDF (`Transfer of Trainng in Sports - Bondarchuk.pdf`, 236 pp.,
real text layer), not the Golden image scan. I extracted the text layer page by page with
PyMuPDF using the same 0-based index as the entries, checked every quote and number against it,
and opened load-bearing pages as images with the Read tool (viewer 38, 77, 164) to confirm the
text layer matches the printed page. **Locators below are written "PDF n (viewer n+1) / p. X"**,
where PDF n is the entries' 0-based index and printed p. = PDF - 17 in the body (PDF 18 = p. 1).
Front matter: PDF 2 = i, so PDF 12 = xi, PDF 14 = xiii.

**Confidence check.** No entry uses `proven`. Every `supported` / `untested` rating is within the
brief's cap for translated Soviet-era work. No confidence row is changed except where noted
(`contested` for a source contradiction).

**Duplicates.** No vault entry restates any of the 19 without a new angle. Closest overlap:
vault `fundamentals-of-sprinting--moyer/framework--sprint-exercise-classes-bondarchuk-four-categories.md`
(secondary paraphrase of the four classes; the Bondarchuk entry is the primary source, so it
is a new angle). The Moyer `principle--sprint-transfer-motor-ability-vs-motor-skill.md` covers
Thorndike's identical elements; `framework--three-viewpoints-on-training-transfer` adds the
generalist/holistic debate, so it is also new. Reciprocal links: Moyer four-categories entry
and Moyer `claim--exercise-selection-over-intensity-volume-sprint.md` (which quotes the PDF 24
"unnecessary muscle groups" passage second-hand) should point back here after promotion.

## Cross-cutting problems (apply to most rows; fix once, everywhere)

1. **Population is misstated as Soviet-only.** Nearly every entry says "Soviet" or "Soviet-era"
   athletes, and `_book.md` says the corpus is "entirely within the USSR system." The source
   says otherwise: "learning-training groups which included not only native, but foreign
   athletes" and "More than 7,000 athletes having different sports qualifications were
   examined" (PDF 8 (viewer 9) / p. vii); "The data used was received mainly through the use of
   questionnaires from native and foreign athletes having different sports qualifications.
   The questionnaires were carried out over the course of four Olympic cycles. Also analyzed
   were tests results of individual athletes as recorded in different literature sources"
   (PDF 76 (viewer 77) / p. 59). Table 8 lists L. Evans, T. Smith, M. Cox and Bulgarian athletes
   (PDF 48 / p. 31). **Correction for every "When NOT to apply":** "Population: native (USSR) and
   foreign track and field athletes of mixed qualification, data mainly from questionnaires
   over four Olympic cycles plus published individual results (PDF 8 / p. vii; PDF 76 / p. 59)."
   Keep "not football, not team sport."
2. **The significance threshold is never stated.** "A positive interrelationship between
   exercises begins at 0.349" (PDF 76 / p. 59); women's pole vault uses 0.423 (PDF 111 / p. 94).
   Every Chapter 2 claim entry quotes coefficients without it. Add one line to each claim entry
   (and to `heuristic--correlation-methodology-limits-and-tie-in-effect`).
3. **Non-steroid restriction.** The preface limits the data to "training systems without the use
   of steroids" and says steroid use raises results in all exercises, masking transfer
   (PDF 9 (viewer 10) / p. viii). This is a scope condition on every correlation; add it to the
   methodology heuristic at minimum.
4. **Unlabelled application examples.** The brief forbids invented examples without a label.
   Nine entries give an invented football or event example in plain text (listed per row).
   Correction in each case: prefix the Example with "Inference:".
5. **`_book.md` errors (outside the 19 but blocking for the next batch).** (a) "entirely within
   the USSR system" (see 1). (b) "PDF pages 52-65 ... pure normative tables, no narrative prose"
   is false: Tables 1-34 end at PDF 60; PDF 60-65 carry prose plus Tables 35-40 (implement
   weight difference norms), and PDF 64-67 carry the section's conclusions (PDF 61-65 / pp. 44-48).
   (c) The row "1.g Model Characteristics (Tables 1-34)" should read Tables 1-40.

## Entry table

| File | Verdict | Problem (entry vs source, with page) | Exact correction |
|---|---|---|---|
| `framework--bondarchuk-four-exercise-classes.md` | FIX | (1) Voice. The entry treats the Glossary as "the book's" and argues it is probably Bondarchuk's. The Glossary contains translator voice: "In the U.S., these terms are most often used interchangeably" and "The physical education discipline is more highly developed and scientific in the Russian literature than in the U.S." (PDF 13 (viewer 14) / p. xii); "This is a unique term that has no analogy in the English language" (Motor Analyzer, same page). The task rule: a translator (Yessis) voice is not the author's. (2) Abbreviations. The entry labels "Specialized-Preparatory Exercises / SPP", "SDE", "CE". The Glossary attaches "SPP" to a different term, "Specialized Exercises ... Also known as specialized physical preparation (SPP)" (PDF 14 / p. xiii); "SDE" and "CE" are not in the Glossary. (3) Example is unlabelled and conflicts with the author: "general preparatory = general conditioning running" for a shot putter, while Bondarchuk says short runs for throwers are specialized-preparatory and calls classifying middle/long-distance running as general "Even more surprising" (PDF 24 (viewer 25) / p. 7). (4) Population line (cross-cutting 1). Quotes checked: GPP at PDF 12 / p. xi, SPE and SDE at PDF 14 / p. xiii, CE at PDF 11-12 / pp. x-xi, local vs global at PDF 75 / p. 58: all correct. | Replace the voice note with: "The Glossary is unsigned and contains lines in the translator's voice (U.S. comparisons, PDF 13 / p. xii). Treat the definitions as the translated edition's, possibly Yessis's glosses; Bondarchuk's own usage is in Chapter 1-2 prose (e.g. PDF 24 / p. 7; PDF 62 / p. 45, 'we did not take exercises from the general developmental group')." Drop "SPP/SDE/CE" as Glossary labels or mark them "this entry's abbreviations"; note that the Glossary's "SPP" glosses "Specialized Exercises". Rewrite the Example as "Inference:" and use Bondarchuk's own placement: short sprints, barbell clean/snatch, half squat = specialized-preparatory for throwers (PDF 24 / p. 7); lighter/heavier implement throws = specialized-developmental (PDF 62 / p. 45; PDF 69 / p. 52); pick a general example the author does not reclassify, or say he gives none. |
| `framework--current-vs-distant-training-transfer.md` | NO-GO | Reverses the author's conclusion. Entry: "Bondarchuk proposes that ... the achieved level from a previous stage can transfer to the following stage in one of three ways" (start / middle / end). Source: the three are "situations" one "can encounter" in "sports practice" (PDF 35 (viewer 36) / p. 18); his own conclusion is the opposite: "we came to the conclusion that the transfer ... takes place **not at the beginning, middle or end** of each of the following stages, blocks, **but over the duration of them**" (PDF 37 (viewer 38) / p. 20, opened as image). (4) "the underlying logic ... is directly portable" is an unlabelled judgment. (5) Wide-receiver Example is invented and unlabelled. Checked correct: general-test list incl. Abalakov jump (PDF 68 / p. 51); "tightened up in the near future" (PDF 69 / p. 52); no reference number given. | Rewrite the two bullets as: general tests (shared across events) vs specialized tests (event-specific); then a separate sentence: "Of tests generally, the reliability of SDE tests (lighter/heavier implements, short-approach jumps, set segments at set speed and rest) 'has already been shown'; GP and SP test reliability 'not fully confirmed' (PDF 68-69 / pp. 51-52)." Add "The competitive exercise is the most important test (PDF 68 / p. 51)." Delete "as transfer indicators". Prefix "directly portable" sentence and the Example with "Inference:". Fix population. |

Source: he names the block method (PDF 28 (viewer 29) / p. 11, ref [49]) and then says "there is a theoretical and practical error working at the base of the artificial division of form and content" (same page). The entry drops the criticism. (2) Omits the holistic deficiency he names: athletes peak first in non-specific exercises and "the level of trainedness decreases long before entering the state of sports form in the specialized exercises" (PDF 28 / p. 11). # Review: Bondarchuk, *Transfer of Training in Sports* Vol I, Chapters 1-2 (round 1, Opus)

Reviewer: independent round-1 reviewer (Opus), 2026-09-27. Scope: all 19 entries in
`staging/library/strength-and-conditioning/transfer-of-training-in-sports--bondarchuk/`.
Read-only on entries and source.

**Method.** Source: the Yessis text PDF (`Transfer of Trainng in Sports - Bondarchuk.pdf`, 236 pp.,
real text layer), not the Golden image scan. I extracted the text layer page by page with
PyMuPDF using the same 0-based index as the entries, checked every quote and number against it,
and opened load-bearing pages as images with the Read tool (viewer 38, 77, 164) to confirm the
text layer matches the printed page. **Locators below are written "PDF n (viewer n+1) / p. X"**,
where PDF n is the entries' 0-based index and printed p. = PDF - 17 in the body (PDF 18 = p. 1).
Front matter: PDF 2 = i, so PDF 12 = xi, PDF 14 = xiii.

**Confidence check.** No entry uses `proven`. Every `supported` / `untested` rating is within the
brief's cap for translated Soviet-era work. No confidence row is changed except where noted
(`contested` for a source contradiction).

**Duplicates.** No vault entry restates any of the 19 without a new angle. Closest overlap:
vault `fundamentals-of-sprinting--moyer/framework--sprint-exercise-classes-bondarchuk-four-categories.md`
(secondary paraphrase of the four classes; the Bondarchuk entry is the primary source, so it
is a new angle). The Moyer `principle--sprint-transfer-motor-ability-vs-motor-skill.md` covers
Thorndike's identical elements; `framework--three-viewpoints-on-training-transfer` adds the
generalist/holistic debate, so it is also new. Reciprocal links: Moyer four-categories entry
and Moyer `claim--exercise-selection-over-intensity-volume-sprint.md` (which quotes the PDF 24
"unnecessary muscle groups" passage second-hand) should point back here after promotion.

## Cross-cutting problems (apply to most rows; fix once, everywhere)

1. **Population is misstated as Soviet-only.** Nearly every entry says "Soviet" or "Soviet-era"
   athletes, and `_book.md` says the corpus is "entirely within the USSR system." The source
   says otherwise: "learning-training groups which included not only native, but foreign
   athletes" and "More than 7,000 athletes having different sports qualifications were
   examined" (PDF 8 (viewer 9) / p. vii); "The data used was received mainly through the use of
   questionnaires from native and foreign athletes having different sports qualifications.
   The questionnaires were carried out over the course of four Olympic cycles. Also analyzed
   were tests results of individual athletes as recorded in different literature sources"
   (PDF 76 (viewer 77) / p. 59). Table 8 lists L. Evans, T. Smith, M. Cox and Bulgarian athletes
   (PDF 48 / p. 31). **Correction for every "When NOT to apply":** "Population: native (USSR) and
   foreign track and field athletes of mixed qualification, data mainly from questionnaires
   over four Olympic cycles plus published individual results (PDF 8 / p. vii; PDF 76 / p. 59)."
   Keep "not football, not team sport."
2. **The significance threshold is never stated.** "A positive interrelationship between
   exercises begins at 0.349" (PDF 76 / p. 59); women's pole vault uses 0.423 (PDF 111 / p. 94).
   Every Chapter 2 claim entry quotes coefficients without it. Add one line to each claim entry
   (and to `heuristic--correlation-methodology-limits-and-tie-in-effect`).
3. **Non-steroid restriction.** The preface limits the data to "training systems without the use
   of steroids" and says steroid use raises results in all exercises, masking transfer
   (PDF 9 (viewer 10) / p. viii). This is a scope condition on every correlation; add it to the
   methodology heuristic at minimum.
4. **Unlabelled application examples.** The brief forbids invented examples without a label.
   Nine entries give an invented football or event example in plain text (listed per row).
   Correction in each case: prefix the Example with "Inference:".
5. **`_book.md` errors (outside the 19 but blocking for the next batch).** (a) "entirely within
   the USSR system" (see 1). (b) "PDF pages 52-65 ... pure normative tables, no narrative prose"
   is false: Tables 1-34 end at PDF 60; PDF 60-65 carry prose plus Tables 35-40 (implement

Reviewer: independent round-1 reviewer (Opus), 2026-09-27. Scope: all 19 entries in
`staging/library/strength-and-conditioning/transfer-of-training-in-sports--bondarchuk/`.
Read-only on entries and source.

**Method.** Source: the Yessis text PDF (`Transfer of Trainng in Sports - Bondarchuk.pdf`, 236 pp.,
real text layer), not the Golden image scan. I extracted the text layer page by page with
PyMuPDF using the same 0-based index as the entries, checked every quote and number against it,
and opened load-bearing pages as images with the Read tool (viewer 38, 77, 164) to confirm the
text layer matches the printed page. **Locators below are written "PDF n (viewer n+1) / p. X"**,

brief's cap for translated Soviet-era work. No confidence row is changed except where noted
(`contested` for a source contradiction).

vault `fundamentals-of-sprinting--moyer/framework--sprint-exercise-classes-bondarchuk-four-categories.md`

## Cross-cutting problems (apply to most rows; fix once, everywhere)

1. **Population is misstated as Soviet-only.** Nearly every entry says "Soviet" or "Soviet-era"
   athletes, and `_book.md` says the corpus is "entirely within the USSR system." The source

   over four Olympic cycles plus published individual results (PDF 8 / p. vii; PDF 76 / p. 59)."

   methodology heuristic at minimum.

   sports form development (PDF 7 / p. vi; PDF 73 / p. 56). Candidate principle entry.

   muscle groups.** Short runs for jumpers and throwers, the barbell clean and half squat are

   (PDF 24-25 / pp. 7-8). His study took no general-developmental exercises at all (PDF 62 / p. 45).

I've finished the round-1 review of all 19 Bondarchuk Ch1-2 entries. **Counts: GO 0, FIX 16, NO-GO 3. Overall verdict: GO AFTER FIXES**, not PROMOTE, because the three NO-GO entries must be rewritten, not patched.

**How I checked.** I pulled the text of the Yessis PDF page by page and checked every quote and number against it. I also opened three key pages with the Read tool (viewer 38, 77 and 164). No entry uses `proven`, so the confidence ratings are within the caps. No entry duplicates a vault entry; the nearest is the Moyer four-categories entry, and this one is the primary source for it.

**The three NO-GO entries.** Each states a rule the author contradicts on a page I opened:
- `framework--current-vs-distant-training-transfer`: it says Bondarchuk proposes that transfer happens at the start, middle or end of the next stage. He lists those as situations seen in practice, then concludes transfer happens "not at the beginning, middle or end ... but over the duration of them", and only when the exercises continue through the stages (PDF 37-38 / pp. 20-21).
- `claim--aerobic-anaerobic-energy-system-transfer-asymmetry`: it says aerobic work may build a base for anaerobic-alactate work. The source says aerobic loads "do not show an influence" on alactate sports form and that aerobic work hurts speed (PDF 163 / p. 146). The book also states the alactate-aerobic time-to-form effect three different ways (PDF 164, 165, 173), so the entry needs `contested`.
- `framework--transfer-chain-general-to-competitive`: it says transfer runs as a chain and only the two most specific exercise classes transfer directly to competition. PDF 33 / p. 16 names general exercises acting on competitive ones directly, and also the reverse direction. The entry also inverts the long-jump example: the source says full- or short-run-up jumps improve 30 m / 60 m speed.

**Problems across most entries:**
- **Population.** Nearly every entry, and `_book.md`, says the athletes were Soviet only. The source says "native and foreign athletes", 7,000+, surveyed by questionnaire over four Olympic cycles (PDF 8 / p. vii; PDF 76 / p. 59).
- **Correlation threshold.** No entry says the book counts a correlation as positive from r = 0.349 (PDF 76 / p. 59).
- **Data scope.** No entry says the data come only from training without steroids (PDF 9 / p. viii).
- **Unlabelled examples.** About ten entries give invented football or event examples in plain text instead of labelling them "Inference:".

**Notable FIX items:**
- `claim--three-types-of-training-transfer`: "indifferent" transfer is the double-effect case, and the book takes the term from the literature. The entry equates it with neutral and calls it Bondarchuk's own category.
- `principle--conjugated-training-effects`: the "Menkhin, not Verkhoshansky" lineage discrepancy is invented. The text says "other specialists" and names no one.
- `heuristic--correlation-methodology-limits-and-tie-in-effect`: the A-B correlation was "sufficiently high", not unremarkable. The author does give an explanation (brain-level integration), and he calls the situation one that "frequently arise[s]".
- `claim--jump-event-exercise-transfer-patterns`: the women's 10-fold jump range should start at 0.865, not 0.886. The book contradicts itself on high jump, and the entry resolves that without saying so. The barbell snatch claim is wrong.
- `claim--model-characteristic-tables-exist-by-qualification`: the section holds Tables 1-40, not 1-34. The entry says Speed Reserve can't be derived, but it can: 400 m time / 4 minus 100 m time (Evans 0.765, T. Smith 0.825, Carr 1.150).
- `claim--throws-implement-weight-transfer-near-universal`: it misses the 10-20% implement-weight band, a third exception and the right page for the 35/38 count.
- `claim--throws-strength-exercise-ceiling-effect`: the ceilings are competition-distance bands, but the entry treats them as strength numbers.
- `framework--bondarchuk-four-exercise-classes`: the Glossary contains lines in the translator's voice (the U.S. comparisons on PDF 13 / p. xii).

**`_book.md` (outside the 19, but the next batch resumes from it).** Besides the population error, it wrongly says PDF 52-65 is "pure tables, no prose". That range has prose and Tables 35-40.

**Missing ideas (5):**
1. The method, the 0.349 threshold and the steroid exclusion.
2. Transfer needs the exercises to continue through the stages, and needs gains in those exercises.
3. Bondarchuk reclassifies common "general" work as specialized-preparatory and warns that building unneeded muscle groups transfers negatively.
4. Implement-weight dosing: the 10-20% band, Tables 35-40, and the excess-volume "throwing boom" warning.
5. In endurance events, correlation rises as the training distance nears the race distance; and hitting test norms, even in the specialized-developmental exercises, "does not guarantee" gains in the main event.

I wrote only the report file. Two scratch files for the page-text search sit in my temp folder, outside the repo.
